summary.intent: Execute a two-wave cleanup to remove dead vault migration code from both the API (backend) and client (frontend/desktop) layers.
summary.outcome: Wave 1 (20-05) completed successfully, removing the vault migration DB columns, endpoint, and service method. Wave 2 (20-06) was initiated via a spawned agent to clean up the client-side migration code paths.

repo: Vault migration involved a PATH A (IPFS v2 blob) and PATH B (DB decrypt + lazy migration) split in the web login flow
Desktop Rust code had a parallel non-migrated branch in fetch_and_decrypt_vault and crypto fields in InitVaultRequest
API client types are regenerated from the backend, so backend changes (Wave 1) must complete before client type cleanup (Wave 2) can proceed
Vault entity/DTOs were simplified down to only ownerPublicKey + rootIpnsName after removing migration fields
workflow: Waves were sequenced with explicit dependency checks (pre-wave dependency check) before proceeding
A spot-check pattern was used to verify artifacts (SUMMARY file, commits, migration file) before moving to the next wave
Controller spec alignment required a 1 auto-fix deviation, suggesting tests were not fully in sync with the implementation before cleanup

friction: Wave 2 depends on regenerated API client types from Wave 1, creating a hard sequencing constraint between waves
1 auto-fix deviation was needed for controller spec alignment in Wave 1, indicating a minor test/implementation drift
open_items: Wave 2 (20-06) client cleanup was spawned but not yet confirmed complete — covers web login PATH B removal, DB fallback removal, v2 blob publish on new vault init, Rust non-migrated branch removal, and recovery tool null handling cleanup
